title: Decompose plans by user-facing jobs, not by how the system is built

facts.note: Needs a phase observer that knows the agent is decomposing work into plans, wagons, WMBTs or acceptances rather than writing code.
Planning artifacts are identifiable by path/file kind.
Task text names a planning/decomposition activity.

values: plan item not stated as a user-facing job the system performs
facts.note: Whether a plan item describes what the system does for a user (vs. how it is built, or any other non-user-facing framing) requires semantic judgement; implementation-flavored sources are one specific case.

fires: A planner decomposes any feature request or source material into plan items (wagons/WMBTs/acceptances).
A source or draft plan item reads like an implementation decision (e.g. 'use redis for caching').
A draft plan item describes an internal mechanism, component or objective rather than a job the user gets done, even if it is not a technology choice.
doesNotFire: Authoring an ADR or test that records a technology choice routed there from planning.
Coding work that implements an already-decomposed plan.

given: A planner is decomposing sources into plan items (wagons, WMBTs, acceptances).
then: Each plan item states what the system does — a user-facing job it performs (domain capability) — not how it is built.
prefer: Reframe an implementation-flavored source to the user-facing job it serves: 'use redis for caching' becomes 'browse catalog pages with instant response'.
Alternatively, route an implementation decision (technology choice) to tests/ADRs instead of the plan.
Do this reframing before writing the job statement, so the job grammar operates on user-facing jobs.
avoid: Plan items describing how the system is built instead of what it does for the user.
Keeping implementation-flavored source text as a plan item instead of reframing it to a user-facing job or routing it to tests/ADRs.
why: The plan decomposes what the system does (user-facing jobs), not how it is built; implementation decisions belong reframed to the job they serve or in tests/ADRs.
evidence: Each plan item reads as a user-facing job the system performs (domain capability), not as how the system is built.
Every implementation-flavored source item is traceable either to a reframed user-facing job or to a test/ADR it was routed to.
verifier_detail: Term domain_capability: a user-facing job the system performs.
Term technology_choice: an implementation decision; reframed to the job it serves or routed to tests/ADRs.
Detection is LLM-judged; canonical example: 'use redis for caching' -> 'browse catalog pages with instant response'.
